title: Using AI in the Classroom
text:
Transparency starts with the instructor: if you use AI to build course materials, say so, the same way you'd expect a student to.

Declaring AI use in a submission is about attribution, not permission-seeking — and a student should never be penalized for AI use that was explicitly allowed.

The strongest classroom activities make AI's reasoning (and its limits) visible: comparing an AI output to a primary source, requiring prompts to be submitted alongside the work, having peers critique an AI-generated answer.
